bands.name: Superior glenohumeral ligament
bands.mechanical_role: resists inferior translation and external rotation with the arm adducted
bands.function_note: The most consistently present but mechanically least significant of the three glenohumeral ligaments in the adducted position.
bands.source: Turkel SJ, Panio MW, Marshall JL, Girgis FG (1981) 'Stabilizing mechanisms preventing anterior dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 63(8):1208-1217 -- classic description of the inferior glenohumeral ligament's anterior band/axillary pouch/posterior band and their reciprocal tensioning with arm position.

bands.name: Middle glenohumeral ligament

attachments.landmark_b: lesser tubercle, medial to bicipital groove

bands.mechanical_role: resists anterior translation and external rotation with the arm at ~45 degrees abduction
bands.function_note: Highly variable in size and presence (absent in a documented minority of shoulders); a well-known source of anatomical variation.
bands.source: Turkel SJ, Panio MW, Marshall JL, Girgis FG (1981) 'Stabilizing mechanisms preventing anterior dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 63(8):1208-1217 -- classic description of the inferior glenohumeral ligament's anterior band/axillary pouch/posterior band and their reciprocal tensioning with arm position.

bands.name: Inferior glenohumeral ligament, anterior band
bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint to anterior/inferior dislocation with the arm abducted and externally rotated
bands.function_note: Tightens with abduction+external rotation while the posterior band slackens -- the classic hammock/pouch mechanism.
bands.source: Turkel SJ, Panio MW, Marshall JL, Girgis FG (1981) 'Stabilizing mechanisms preventing anterior dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 63(8):1208-1217 -- classic description of the inferior glenohumeral ligament's anterior band/axillary pouch/posterior band and their reciprocal tensioning with arm position.

bands.name: Inferior glenohumeral ligament, posterior band
bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint to posterior dislocation with the arm abducted and internally rotated
bands.function_note: Tightens with abduction+internal rotation while the anterior band slackens, together with the axillary pouch forming the sling that cradles the humeral head in abduction.
bands.source: Turkel SJ, Panio MW, Marshall JL, Girgis FG (1981) 'Stabilizing mechanisms preventing anterior dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 63(8):1208-1217 -- classic description of the inferior glenohumeral ligament's anterior band/axillary pouch/posterior band and their reciprocal tensioning with arm position.

function: The three glenohumeral ligaments are capsular thickenings (not free-standing cords) that provide the shoulder's primary static restraint against dislocation, complementing the rotator cuff's dynamic stabilization.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Turkel SJ, Panio MW, Marshall JL, Girgis FG (1981) 'Stabilizing mechanisms preventing anterior dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 63(8):1208-1217 -- classic description of the inferior glenohumeral ligament's anterior band/axillary pouch/posterior band and their reciprocal tensioning with arm position.

attachments.landmark_b: greater and lesser tubercles (forms the roof of the biceps tendon sheath/rotator interval)

bands.name: Coracohumeral ligament
bands.mechanical_role: reinforces the rotator interval and resists inferior translation with the arm adducted; restrains external rotation
bands.function_note: Bridges the rotator interval between supraspinatus and subscapularis, alongside the superior glenohumeral ligament.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: Reinforces the rotator-interval capsule and helps suspend the humeral head, especially with the arm at the side.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Coracoacromial ligament
bands.mechanical_role: forms the coracoacromial arch, a protective roof over the rotator cuff and subacromial bursa
bands.function_note: Uniquely a bone-to-bone ligament spanning two processes of the SAME bone (scapula) rather than bridging two separate bones; clinically important in subacromial impingement.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: Together with the coracoid and acromion forms the coracoacromial arch protecting the underlying supraspinatus tendon and subacromial bursa.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

attachments.landmark_a: conoid tubercle / trapezoid line, inferior clavicle

bands.name: Conoid ligament
bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint against superior/anterior displacement of the clavicle at the AC joint; primary vertical stabilizer
bands.function_note: The stronger, more vertically-oriented of the two CC ligament bands.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Trapezoid ligament
bands.mechanical_role: resists axial/horizontal compression forces at the AC joint, secondary to the conoid
bands.function_note: The more horizontally-oriented, quadrilateral band, lateral to the conoid ligament.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The principal vertical stabilizer of the acromioclavicular joint -- its rupture (not just the weaker AC ligament's) defines the higher grades of AC joint separation (Rockwood III+).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Acromioclavicular ligament
bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint against posterior and horizontal displacement of the clavicle at the AC joint
bands.function_note: A capsular thickening (superior part is the strongest) distinct from and weaker than the coracoclavicular ligament, which is the joint's primary vertical stabilizer.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: Provides horizontal/posterior stability at the small, often-injured acromioclavicular joint; the primary structure disrupted in low-grade AC separations.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Anterior sternoclavicular ligament
bands.mechanical_role: resists anterior translation of the medial clavicle
bands.function_note: Broad, flat capsular band on the anterior joint surface.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Posterior sternoclavicular ligament
bands.mechanical_role: resists posterior translation of the medial clavicle; considered the strongest single restraint at this joint
bands.function_note: Posterior displacement of the medial clavicle (a rare but dangerous injury given the retrosternal great vessels) is resisted primarily by this band.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The sternoclavicular joint's main capsular ligaments; together with the costoclavicular and interclavicular ligaments they make traumatic SC dislocation rare relative to the anatomically small, incongruent joint surfaces.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

attachments.landmark_a: 1st rib, superior surface near costal cartilage

bands.name: Costoclavicular ligament
bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint limiting clavicular elevation and acting as the pivot for clavicular rotation during arm elevation
bands.function_note: Short, strong, rhomboid-shaped ligament that functions as the fulcrum around which the clavicle rotates during scapulohumeral rhythm.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: Anchors the clavicle to the first rib and functions as the mechanical pivot for clavicular elevation/rotation during arm movement.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Interclavicular ligament
bands.mechanical_role: connects both sternoclavicular joint capsules across the jugular (suprasternal) notch, resisting downward displacement of the shoulder girdle
bands.function_note: A single unpaired band spanning both clavicles over the top of the manubrium -- unusual among ligaments in bridging two mirror-image bones directly rather than a bone to its neighbor.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: Links the two sternoclavicular joints, helping suspend the shoulder girdle and limiting excessive depression of either shoulder.
